_note: Only the owner edits this file. Every row carries saudiDataTier and a source citation with n and table number. Tier 1 frequencies are verbatim from Goljan et al. 2022 Table 1. Never substitute global, European, or Gulf-neighbour frequencies into Tier 2 genes.
_coverageStatement: Saudi allele frequencies for Tier 1 genes (CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP3A5, CYP4F2, VKORC1, DPYD, TPMT, NUDT15) come directly from Goljan et al. (PLoS ONE 2022;17(1):e0263137, Table 1), representing 11,889 unrelated Saudi nationals (9,961 exomes and 1,928 PGx panels) sequenced in the Saudi Human Genome Program (2015-2019). Genes without published Saudi allele frequencies (Tier 2, such as SLCO1B1) return null risk rather than borrowing non-Saudi figures, and CYP2D6 (Tier 0) receives no A5 score because structural variants were excluded from that study and are gated by A8.
_cautions: Raw SHGP data are not public ('Data cannot be shared publicly because of National policy'); only published Table 1 values are cited.
Goljan et al. 2022 reports CYP3A5*3 as 84.5% in Table 1 and 84.7% in the Results text; this table uses Table 1 (84.5%).
The paper's abstract and results disagree on the rare-variant count, so that figure is intentionally omitted.
